question.text: Where will the USS Theodore Roosevelt be on December 1, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves as the location of the USS Theodore Roosevelt, according to the most recent update published before December 2, 2026 by the [USNI News Fleet and Marine Tracker](https://news.usni.org/category/fleet-tracker). For purposes of this question, "location" is defined as the body of water on which the vessel sits, according to the Tracker.

The options cover these areas:

1. **Pacific and Southeast Asian seas:** the Philippine Sea, East China Sea, Sea of Japan, Taiwan Strait, South China Sea, Singapore Strait, or other Pacific Ocean or Southeast Asian waters east of the Strait of Malacca not covered by options 2–4.
2. **Other Indian Ocean waters outside CENTCOM:** the Strait of Malacca, Andaman Sea, Bay of Bengal, or other Indian Ocean waters outside the CENTCOM area of responsibility and not covered by option 1 or 3.
3. **Arabian Sea:** the Arabian Sea, including the North Arabian Sea, but excluding the Gulf of Oman and Gulf of Aden.
4. **Gulf of Oman and other CENTCOM waters:** the Gulf of Oman, Red Sea, Gulf of Aden, Persian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz, or other waters within the CENTCOM maritime area of responsibility not covered by option 3.
5. **Any other outcome:** any location not covered by options 1–4, or insufficient information to determine the vessel’s position, as specified in the Fine Print.
question.fine_print:
If the text provides no specific body of water or only offers a vague phrase such as "Western Pacific" or "Indo-Pacific,", the question resolves as the vessel's location on the map graphic.

If for any reason the tracker has no mention of the vessel or offers no information on its position in its most recent update as of the target date, or the vessel is located in none of the other options, then the question resolves as **Any other outcome**.

In case of issues accessing the resolution source, the question may resolve according to [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).

Specifically-named seas and straits take precedence over any broader regional descriptions

research:
I couldn't open the resolving source: news.usni.org returned HTTP 403. All USNI tracker information below comes from secondary summaries. Nothing settles the question yet. As of November 2 to 6 the carrier was in or near the South China Sea and headed for Singapore, and then for the Middle East.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-06: The [Fleet Tracker archive](https://news.usni.org/category/fleet-tracker) and the [Nov. 2 tracker](https://news.usni.org/2026/11/02/usni-news-fleet-and-marine-tracker-nov-2-2026) both returned HTTP 403, so I could not read them directly.
- 2026-11-02: According to a [Ghost Fleet Journal summary](https://ghostfleet.substack.com/p/fleet-watch-2026-11-03) of that tracker:
  - USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71) was in the **South China Sea** after the Keen Sword 27 exercise (option 1).
  - USS George Washington and USS George H.W. Bush were in the **Arabian Sea**, supporting Middle East operations.
- 2026-11-05: [USNI's own report on USS Stout](https://news.usni.org/2026/11/05/uss-stout-loses-power-during-port-visit-due-to-engineering-casualty) cites "Monday's" tracker, which confirms Nov. 2 is the latest tracker.
- Trackers usually come out on Mondays. Nov. 30, 2026 is a Monday, so the Nov. 30 tracker will probably decide the question, unless an update is published Dec. 1.

## 2. Current status
- Not settled. The carrier was in the Pacific/Southeast Asia area (option 1) as of early November. Every report says it is heading to CENTCOM.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-06: Reports citing Barak Ravid of Axios say:
  - The strike group (Roosevelt plus four ships) will stop in Singapore for several days, then go on to the Middle East.
  - It will reach the CENTCOM area **no earlier than mid-November**.
  - Sources differ on whether the Singapore stop starts Thursday Nov. 5 or Friday Nov. 6. [EADaily](https://eadaily.com/en/news/2026/11/06/the-united-states-sent-an-aircraft-carrier-group-to-the-middle-east), [Interfax](https://www.interfax.ru/world/1127306)
- 2026-11-05: Axios reports that Trump met his national security team and says a decision on resuming large-scale strikes on Iran is coming "soon." [Axios](https://axios.com/2026/11/05/trump-iran-war-national-security-team-decision) (I could not open the page, so this comes from the search snippet and the news summaries.)
- 2026-11-04: MizarVision satellite imagery and Al Jazeera place the carrier, with USS Chosin and USS Roosevelt (DDG-80), near the Spratly Islands in the South China Sea. [Zona Militar](https://www.zona-militar.com/2026/11/04/china-sigue-de-cerca-al-portaaviones-uss-theodore-roosevelt-en-el-mar-del-sur-de-china/), [SETN](https://www.setn.com/news/1934335)
- Late October 2026: The carrier was in the Philippine Sea for Keen Sword 27, after a port call at Yokosuka that ended Oct. 19 (TWZ, from the question background).
- 2026-09-27/28: Roosevelt left San Diego (Carrier Strike Group 9, Carrier Air Wing 11).
  - It is expected to relieve USS George Washington in CENTCOM.
  - Families were told to expect about 8 months away.
  - The Iran war began Feb. 28, 2026.
  - [Task & Purpose](https://taskandpurpose.com/news/roosevelt-carrier-iran-war-deployment/), [Ynet](https://www.ynetnews.com/article/h1wsyz35fx)

## 4. Base rates and transit logic
- Singapore to the North Arabian Sea through the Strait of Malacca is roughly 3,000 nautical miles. At typical transit speeds that is about 6 to 9 days.
  - If the port call lasts about 3 to 5 days, the carrier would leave Singapore around Nov. 9 to 11.
  - That timing is consistent with entering CENTCOM in mid-to-late November and being well inside it by Nov. 30. This is my own estimate, not a sourced figure.
- On the way it would pass through the Strait of Malacca and the Indian Ocean (option 2) for about a week.
- Recent precedent for where carriers sit inside CENTCOM: the Nov. 2 tracker put both Washington and Bush in the **Arabian Sea**. During the 2026 Iran operations, carriers have usually been listed in the Arabian Sea or North Arabian Sea, not the Gulf of Oman or Red Sea. I did not check older trackers to confirm this.
- Risks that would change the timeline:
  - The Singapore stop runs long.
  - The carrier is held in the South China Sea or Indian Ocean if the Iran decision changes.
  - A longer stop elsewhere, such as Diego Garcia, though I found no report of one.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket, "USS Theodore Roosevelt arrives in CENTCOM by...?" (prices as of 2026-11-06 12:03 UTC), Yes probability by date:

| Arrives in CENTCOM by | Yes |
|---|---|
| Nov. 7 | 0.8% |
| Nov. 12 | 2.3% |
| Nov. 15 | 8.5% |
| Nov. 30 | 85% |

  This market is closely related, but it measures arrival in CENTCOM, not which body of water.
- Polymarket, "How many US aircraft carriers in CENTCOM on Nov. 30?": 0 carriers 4%, 1 carrier 7%, 2 carriers 48.5%, 3 carriers 39%, 4 or more 5%. The weight on 3 suggests traders expect Roosevelt to arrive before Washington leaves.
- I found no Metaculus, Manifold or expert forecast on this exact question. The Kalshi markets supplied are unrelated.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The Singapore port call (from about Nov. 5 or 6, lasting "several days"). Its departure date sets the transit timeline.
- Weekly USNI trackers, probably Nov. 9, 16, 23 and 30. These will show the carrier moving through the Strait of Malacca and Indian Ocean.
- Trump's pending decision on resuming strikes on Iran. Strikes could speed up the transit or push the carrier toward the Gulf of Oman. A diplomatic shift could slow it or keep it in the Indian Ocean or Pacific.
- Whether George Washington leaves after being relieved. That could change where Roosevelt is stationed, for example taking over the Arabian Sea position.

Sources: [USNI tracker archive](https://news.usni.org/category/fleet-tracker), [USNI Nov 2 tracker](https://news.usni.org/2026/11/02/usni-news-fleet-and-marine-tracker-nov-2-2026), [Ghost Fleet Journal](https://ghostfleet.substack.com/p/fleet-watch-2026-11-03), [USNI Stout](https://news.usni.org/2026/11/05/uss-stout-loses-power-during-port-visit-due-to-engineering-casualty), [Axios](https://axios.com/2026/11/05/trump-iran-war-national-security-team-decision), [EADaily](https://eadaily.com/en/news/2026/11/06/the-united-states-sent-an-aircraft-carrier-group-to-the-middle-east), [Interfax](https://www.interfax.ru/world/1127306), [Zona Militar](https://www.zona-militar.com/2026/11/04/china-sigue-de-cerca-al-portaaviones-uss-theodore-roosevelt-en-el-mar-del-sur-de-china/), [SETN](https://www.setn.com/news/1934335), [Task & Purpose](https://taskandpurpose.com/news/roosevelt-carrier-iran-war-deployment/), [Ynet](https://www.ynetnews.com/article/h1wsyz35fx)

- The reported destination is the Arabian Sea, where it may relieve USS George Washington on the blockade line. If that happens, the Arabian Sea option fits, but the Gulf of Oman is also a plausible spot within CENTCOM.

## 4. Base rates
- My rough estimate: Singapore to the Arabian Sea is about 2,500 to 3,000 nautical miles, which at typical transit speeds of 15 to 20 knots takes about 6 to 9 days. If the carrier leaves Singapore around Nov 9 to 11, it would plausibly reach the Arabian Sea around Nov 16 to 20. That leaves roughly 10 days of slack before Nov 30.
- The Roosevelt made a similar transit in 2024 and then operated in CENTCOM. I could not find exact dates to calibrate against.
- During the Iran blockade, USNI trackers have generally listed CENTCOM carriers in the Arabian Sea. I have not confirmed how often they used the Gulf of Oman instead.
- The things that could keep it out of CENTCOM by Dec 1 are a longer Singapore stay, a diversion back to the Pacific, or an extended Indian Ocean or Bay of Bengal leg.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket, "USS Theodore Roosevelt arrives in CENTCOM by...?" (fetched 2026-11-06): by Nov 7 0.8%, by Nov 12 2.3%, by Nov 15 8.5%, **by Nov 30 85%**. This matches the question closely, but it measures entering CENTCOM, not which body of water the tracker names.
- Polymarket, "How many US aircraft carriers in CENTCOM on November 30?": 0 at 3.75%, 1 at 7%, 2 at 48.5%, 3 at 39%, 4+ at 4.6%. Three carriers would mean an overlap. Two is also consistent with the Roosevelt having arrived and relieved the George Washington.
- I found no Metaculus community forecast or expert forecast.
- The Kalshi markets in the supplied list are unrelated to this question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Around Nov 6 to 10: Singapore port visit; how long it lasts sets the timeline.
- Mid to late November: Strait of Malacca and Indian Ocean transit. Trackers during this leg (Nov 9, 12, 16, 19, 23) will show where it is, possibly in the Andaman Sea or Bay of Bengal, which fall under the "Indian Ocean outside CENTCOM" option.
- Soon: Trump's decision on resuming Iran strikes. Renewed strikes could speed the transit, while de-escalation could slow it or cancel the overlap.
- The George Washington's relief and departure, which could move carrier positions around between the Arabian Sea and the Gulf of Oman.
- Nov 26: Thanksgiving, which may skip a tracker issue.
- Nov 30 (Monday): probably the tracker issue that decides the question.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** About 24 days. The deciding update is most likely the USNI Fleet Tracker of Monday, Nov. 30, 2026, unless an update is published Dec. 1.

(b) **Status quo:** As of the Nov. 2 tracker and Nov. 4 satellite imagery, Roosevelt was in the South China Sea, which is option 1. However, the status quo here is a planned transit. The carrier is stopping in Singapore and then heading to CENTCOM to relieve USS George Washington. The "status quo trajectory" therefore points to CENTCOM, not the South China Sea.

(c) **Base rates:**
- Carriers sent to relieve another carrier in CENTCOM almost always arrive within about 2 to 3 weeks of leaving Singapore.
- During the 2026 Iran operations, USNI has mostly listed CENTCOM carriers in the Arabian Sea or North Arabian Sea.
- The Gulf of Oman and Red Sea appear less often, perhaps 15 to 25% of carrier-weeks.
- Trackers sometimes lag, or list a carrier in the "Indian Ocean" while it is still in transit.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- Nov. 6: Axios reports a Singapore stop of "several days," then the Middle East, arriving no earlier than mid-November.
- Nov. 4: MizarVision imagery puts the carrier near the Spratly Islands.
- Nov. 5: Trump's decision on resuming strikes on Iran is reportedly coming "soon."
- Nov. 6 Polymarket prices:
  - 85% that Roosevelt arrives in CENTCOM by Nov. 30.
  - The 3-carrier bucket at 39% suggests overlap with Washington.
- Nov. 2 tracker: both carriers already in CENTCOM are listed in the Arabian Sea.

(e) **Unexpected-outcome scenarios:**
- A diplomatic breakthrough with Iran, or a crisis near Taiwan or the South China Sea, keeps Roosevelt in the Pacific.
- An engineering problem or a long Singapore stay delays it in the Indian Ocean or Bay of Bengal.
- Strikes resume and Roosevelt goes to the Gulf of Oman or Red Sea.
- USNI omits the carrier, or labels it vaguely.

**Reasoning:** I anchored on the market's roughly 85% chance of reaching CENTCOM, then trimmed it slightly. The tracker could lag, or describe the carrier as being in the Indian Ocean during the final approach. Within CENTCOM, I give the Arabian Sea about three-quarters of the probability and the Gulf of Oman, Red Sea and similar waters the rest. The rest goes to the Indian Ocean (still in transit), the Pacific (diversion) and other outcomes.

Option_B: 0.14
Option_C: 0.58
Option_D: 0.18
